![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/5453dfc44e11cad377c1e8e2c30fc23d537d4423d38fab4428395362f51d9412.png)

Consider the region bounded by the curve $x={y}^{2}+1,$ the vertical line $x=5,$ and the horizontal line $y=0,$ as shown in the picture. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=5.$

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersection of the curve and the line $x=5$ by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+1 & =5 \\ {y}^{2} & =4 \\ y & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Since $y\ge 0,$ the limits of integration are from $y=0$ to $y=2$ along the $y$-axis.

To determine which is the left and which is the right function, let's draw our horizontal arrow.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/e83c5729ef5db920a0b451a8571ad84f45d2b4e950ab831ced0da2c0a12cea50.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x={y}^{2}+1,$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=5.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}[(\text{right function})-(\text{left function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}[\,5-({y}^{2}+1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(4-{y}^{2})^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(16-8{y}^{2}+{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {(16y-\frac{8}{3}{y}^{3}+\frac{1}{5}{y}^{5})|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\pi (32-\frac{64}{3}+\frac{32}{5}) \\  & =\frac{256\pi }{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
